sections.title: Conditional probability: choose the reference group

blocks.text: P(A | B) means the probability of A **among cases in B**. For an equally weighted sample with non-empty B: P(A | B) = count(A and B) / count(B). The denominator is the group after the vertical bar.

blocks.setup: 25 of 40 students commute; 10 commuters cycle. Find the percent of commuters who cycle.
blocks.takeaway: Use the restricted group as denominator; do not divide by all 40 students.

blocks.prompt: Find the percentage of column-group cases with a property.
blocks.first_error: A previous table attempt used a row total for a column percentage.
blocks.fix: Name the reference group first. For a column percentage, divide the cell by that column's total.
blocks.conditions: P(A | B) and P(B | A) generally differ because their reference groups differ.

blocks.text: Report each proportion as a percentage to **one decimal place** and name the reference group: '40.0% of commuters.'

sections.title: Two-way tables: row vs. column percentages

blocks.text: Row % = cell / row total. Column % = cell / column total. This is the same reference-group choice as conditional probability.
Row percentages sum to 100% across each row. Column percentages sum to 100% down each column. Percentages across a row of column percentages need not sum to 100%.
Before dividing, translate the question into words: 'among which group?' Pick that row or column total as the denominator. Report the percentage and name that group.
Split cases by a categorical variable; compute one summary (such as a mean or count) per group.
Output: one row per non-empty group, not one row per original case. Compare groups using the same summary: mean with mean, count with count.
